title: Client Onboarding Checklist: How to Master the Process (+ Free Template)
summary: A step-by-step client onboarding checklist, from signed contract to first results, with the owner of each step and how to turn it into an automated workflow.
body_markdown:
A client onboarding checklist lists every step between a signed contract and the moment a new client sees results, with an owner and a deadline for each. The first 30 days set the tone for the whole relationship, and most onboarding problems come from missed handoffs: sales promised something the delivery team never heard about, or a document sat in someone's inbox for a week. A checklist makes those handoffs visible.


## The client onboarding checklist


### Phase 1: Before kickoff (days 0–3)


- ☐ Contract signed and countersigned; copy stored with the client record.
- ☐ Sales-to-delivery handoff: goals, promises, stakeholders, risks.
- ☐ Client created in CRM, billing and project tools.
- ☐ Account manager and team assigned.
- ☐ Welcome email sent with next steps and key contacts.
- ☐ Portal access created for client contacts.
- ☐ First invoice or deposit issued.


### Phase 2: Information and document collection (days 1–7)


- ☐ Onboarding questionnaire sent: goals, KPIs, brand, systems, contacts.
- ☐ Required documents requested: tax forms, access credentials via a secure method, assets, data exports.
- ☐ Access to client systems granted and tested.
- ☐ Missing items chased automatically after 3 days.


### Phase 3: Kickoff (days 5–10)


- ☐ Kickoff meeting scheduled with all stakeholders.
- ☐ Agenda shared in advance: goals, scope, timeline, roles, communication.
- ☐ Success metrics agreed and written down.
- ☐ Communication plan agreed: channels, meeting cadence, escalation path.
- ☐ Kickoff notes shared within 24 hours.


### Phase 4: Setup and first delivery (days 10–30)


- ☐ Project plan published with milestones.
- ☐ Internal setup completed: workspaces, integrations, reporting.
- ☐ First deliverable shipped (a quick win).
- ☐ Client approval collected on first deliverable.


### Phase 5: Review (day 30)


- ☐ 30-day check-in: progress against goals, feedback, open issues.
- ☐ Onboarding satisfaction survey sent.
- ☐ Handoff to ongoing account management confirmed.
- ☐ Lessons learned added to the onboarding template.


## Checklist template


Turn the checklist into a table so each step has an owner, due date and status:


Step Phase Owner Due (days after signing) Status


Sales-to-delivery handoff Before kickoff Sales rep 1 To do


Welcome email and portal access Before kickoff Account manager 1 To do


Questionnaire and document request Collection Account manager 2 To do


Kickoff meeting Kickoff Account manager 7 To do


Success metrics agreed Kickoff Account manager and client 7 To do


First deliverable Setup Delivery lead 21 To do


30-day review Review Account manager 30 To do


## Tips for a better onboarding


- **Ask for everything once.** One questionnaire and one document list, not ten emails.
- **Show progress.** Clients relax when they can see which steps are done.
- **Deliver a quick win early.** Something tangible in the first two weeks builds trust.
- **Never collect credentials by email.** Use a secure portal or password manager sharing.
- **Automate reminders.** Chasing is the most time-consuming part of onboarding.

## Frequently asked questions


### What should a client onboarding checklist include?


Contract and handoff, account setup, welcome communication, information and document collection, kickoff, success metrics, first delivery and a 30-day review.


### How long should client onboarding take?


For most service businesses, 2–6 weeks, depending on complexity. The first deliverable should arrive within the first few weeks.


### Who owns client onboarding?


Usually an account manager or onboarding specialist, with sales owning the handoff and delivery owning setup.


### How can I automate client onboarding?


Trigger the checklist from your CRM when a deal is won, collect information through a portal, and use workflows for reminders, approvals and notifications.
